title.en: Life in the city: the turning point

heading.en: A bus, an English school and a growing distance

hook.en: When the family moved to the city, the author went to an English school by motor bus. His grandmother could no longer walk with him, and their friendship began to change.

objectives.en: Explain why the city was a turning point in the friendship
Explain the grandmother's views on English education and music
Describe how she coped with loneliness

narration.en: When the family moved to the city, the author went to an English school by motor bus. His grandmother could no longer walk with him, and their friendship began to change.

body.en: In the city the author went to an English school by motor bus, so the grandmother could no longer walk with him. She could not help with his lessons, because she did not understand English, science or ideas such as the law of gravity. She was distressed that the school taught nothing about God and the scriptures. When she learned that he was being taught music, she was deeply upset: in her view music was not for respectable people.

points.en: She could not help with his lessons
Upset: no teaching about God and the scriptures

say.en: Let us compare the two stages side by side.
In the village he went to the temple school; in the city, to an English school.
They walked to school together; in the city he went by bus.
She could help with the village lessons, but not with English and science.
Village dogs are replaced by the city sparrows.
The friendship moves from close companionship to distance.

explanation.en: She accepted her loneliness with quiet dignity; the sparrows became her companions.

title.en: A room of his own, and the sparrows

body.en: When the author went to university he was given a room of his own, and the last thread of their daily companionship broke. The grandmother accepted her loneliness quietly and with dignity. She spent most of the day at her spinning wheel, reciting prayers. Her one pleasure was the afternoon, when she fed the sparrows in the courtyard; they perched on her legs, her shoulders and even her head.

points.en: University: a room of his own
She accepted loneliness with quiet resignation
Spinning wheel and prayers filled her day

narration.en: When the author went to university he was given a room of his own, and the last thread of their daily companionship broke. The grandmother accepted her loneliness quietly and with dignity. She spent most of the day at her spinning wheel, reciting prayers. Her one pleasure was the afternoon, when she fed the sparrows in the courtyard; they perched on her legs, her shoulders and even her head.

problem.en: Why was the grandmother unhappy with the author's education in the city?

steps.en: It taught English, science and the law of gravity, which she did not understand.
It taught nothing about God or the scriptures.
It included music, which she thought unfit for respectable people.

answer.en: The English school taught things she could not understand and nothing about God or the holy books. The music lessons shocked her, as she believed music was not for respectable people. She also could no longer help him, so she felt left out.

At university he got his own room; she found comfort in prayer, spinning and the sparrows.
